title: Proof of the obstruction to $q$-flatness
html:
Item (1). The q-flatness equation is \nabla_q^2 = (q-1)\mathcal{F}_q (q-flat connection). The q-curvature \mathcal{F}_q is a class in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{V}) \otimes \Omega^2_q. The Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg comparison identifies this space with HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}). The image under \mathrm{HKR} is the gerbe-theoretic obstruction class \kappa_0 = e(\xi) (Kummer filtration).

Item (2). If \kappa_0 = 0 in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m), then \mathcal{F}_q = \mathrm{HKR}^{-1}(0) = 0. Thus, \nabla_q is q-flat. Conversely, \mathcal{F}_q = 0 implies \mathrm{HKR}(\mathcal{F}_q) = \kappa_0 = 0.

Item (3). The Kummer exact sequence 1 \to \mu_n \to \mathbb{G}_m \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n} \mathbb{G}_m \to 1 yields the reduction \kappa_0 \bmod n. We know \mathrm{tr}(\kappa_0) = \chi(A). By the Kummer filtration, \kappa_0 \bmod n = 0 if and only if n \mid \chi(A). Lifting through the brane tower from level n to n+1 requires \kappa_n = 0 (Quantum lifting condition). The complementary subgroup structure \kappa_n = \kappa_0 + \delta_n prevents cancellation.

Item (4). The set \{n : n \mid \chi(A)\} has exactly d(\chi(A)) elements, where d is the divisor function. This set is finite. Its complement in \mathbb{Z}_{>0} has density 1. \square
